candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: perform hand hygiene and implement Standard Precautions to prevent transmission of infectious agents.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — hand hygiene and MDRO transmission
candidate.educational_objective: Explain that hand hygiene helps control antimicrobial resistance by interrupting transmission of resistant organisms, while antimicrobial stewardship separately addresses unnecessary or suboptimal antimicrobial exposure.

options.A: Hand hygiene reduces person-to-person transmission of germs, including antimicrobial-resistant organisms, and works alongside antimicrobial stewardship.
options.B: Hand hygiene directly reverses bacterial resistance genes after the organism contacts alcohol-based sanitizer.
options.C: Hand hygiene replaces the need for antimicrobial stewardship because transmission control alone prevents resistance from developing.
options.D: Hand hygiene has little effect on resistant-organism spread because MDRO transmission occurs independently of healthcare workers' hands.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. CDC states that cleaning hands reduces the spread of germs, including those resistant to antibiotics, and identifies healthcare workers' hands as an important route of MDRO transmission. Infection prevention and antimicrobial stewardship address different parts of the resistance problem and are complementary. B is incorrect because hand hygiene removes or kills organisms; it does not genetically reverse resistance. C is incorrect because CDC separately emphasizes preventing spread and improving antibiotic/antifungal use. D contradicts CDC evidence that MDROs can be carried from one person to another via healthcare personnel's hands.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Hand hygiene interrupts transmission of antimicrobial-resistant germs in healthcare settings and complements, rather than replaces, antimicrobial stewardship.
candidate.source_document_title: Clinical Safety: Hand Hygiene for Healthcare Workers; Epidemiology of MDROs; Antimicrobial Resistance: Causes and How It Spreads
candidate.source_locator: Clinical Safety — Why it matters: hand hygiene reduces spread of germs, including those resistant to antibiotics. MDRO Epidemiology — Important concepts in transmission: epidemiologic evidence shows MDROs are carried person-to-person via healthcare personnel's hands and hand-hygiene adherence is an important control component. AR Causes and How It Spreads — prevention requires stopping spread, slowing development, improving antimicrobial use, and preventing infections.
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
